acceptable_variants: warm-condition glacier collapse with direct casualty priority
heat-conditioned serac failure and alpine life-safety priority
primary_gt.canonical_stance: The Marmolada collapse should be prioritized as a heat-conditioned serac-collapse life-safety event, not as rainfall, wind, urban amenity, or vegetation damage.
forbidden_claims: rainfall-triggered flood or GLOF is the primary priority
wind or urban infrastructure disruption is the primary impact interpretation
dNBR or annual embedding change proves burn or vegetation-loss priority
the evidence proves exact collapse volume, runout, or full climate attribution
required_claims: direct report identifies a Marmolada serac collapse on 2022-07-03
direct casualties make life safety the first impact priority
warm high-mountain conditions support cryosphere instability while low point precipitation weakens rainfall-primary explanations
low point wind and the direct incident record weaken wind, urban-service, and vegetation-change framings

criteria.description: Selects heat_conditioned_serac_collapse_life_safety_priority as the compact label for the Marmolada event.
criteria.name: Final classification
criteria.partial_credit: Give partial credit for a serac or glacier-collapse life-safety priority without the exact label; give no credit for rainfall, wind, urban amenity, vegetation, or insufficient-evidence as the primary label.

criteria.description: Reports 11 fatalities, 8 injuries, and a priority_index close to 1.00 as the direct life-safety basis for priority setting.
criteria.name: Casualty and priority anchors
criteria.partial_credit: Give partial credit when the casualty evidence is used correctly but the index is omitted, rounded imprecisely, or not tied to the priority decision.

criteria.description: Connects 12.8 C high-elevation Tmax and 18.8 C same-day point-temperature context to heat-conditioned ice or serac instability without claiming full climate attribution.
criteria.name: Warm-condition cryosphere mechanism
criteria.partial_credit: Give partial credit for mentioning warm conditions without explaining the cryosphere failure mechanism, or for overstating the attribution while preserving the main mechanism.

criteria.description: Uses 0.2 mm high-elevation precipitation, 1.18 mm NASA precipitation, and 7.8 km/h wind to reject rainfall-primary, GLOF-primary, and windstorm-primary interpretations.
criteria.name: Rejection of rainfall and storm alternatives
criteria.partial_credit: Give partial credit for rejecting the alternatives with fewer quantitative anchors while still keeping rainfall and wind secondary.

criteria.description: Keeps urban-service exposure and vegetation or burn-change labels secondary because the confirmed event record is a direct alpine serac-collapse casualty incident.
criteria.name: Alternative-priority control
criteria.partial_credit: Give partial credit for rejecting only one of the urban-service or vegetation-change alternatives.

criteria.description: Gives an impact chain equivalent to warm_high_mountain_conditions -> serac_collapse -> direct_alpine_life_safety.
criteria.name: Impact-chain reasoning
criteria.partial_credit: Give partial credit for a plausible glacier-collapse impact chain that omits either the warm-conditioning driver or the direct life-safety endpoint.

criteria.description: Returns the requested structured answer and avoids unsupported claims about exact collapse volume, runout distance, full climate attribution, or urban service losses.
criteria.name: Format and unsupported-claim control
criteria.partial_credit: Give partial credit for a correct answer with minor formatting issues or a small unsupported statement that does not change the conclusion.
